description: A composite figure of three images: two X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern stacks plus one as-cast micrograph. (a) and (b) are XRD patterns plotted as Intensity (a.u.) versus 2θ (degree) over 30-100°, each stacking four vertically offset diffractograms labelled 'as-cast' (black), '723 K/3 h' (red), '773 K/3 h' (blue) and '823 K/3 h' (green). Panel (a) is titled '0.02Nb steels', panel (b) '0.04Nb steels'. Both display the same reflection set, indexed in the figure as (111)γ, (110)δ, (200)γ, (200)δ, (220)γ, (211)δ, (311)γ and (222)γ; the strongest peaks lie in the lowest-angle cluster, just above the 40° gridline, with weaker reflections near 65°, 82° and 90-95°. Peak positions and relative intensities appear essentially identical across the four aging states and between the two Nb levels. The third image, itself labelled (a), is an as-cast micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar and an 'as-cast' annotation, showing a grey matrix labelled γ with darker, partly lamellar/dendritic regions labelled δ, and yellow and purple arrows marking specific features. Together the panels argue that both Nb steels contain only δ-ferrite and γ-austenite and that aging temperature and Nb content do not measurably change the phase constitution.

observations.observation: Both XRD panels plot intensity in arbitrary units against 2θ in degrees, with the x-axis spanning 30 to 100 in 10° ticks.
Panel (a) is titled '0.02Nb steels' and stacks four diffractograms labelled as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h and 823 K/3 h.
Panel (b) is titled '0.04Nb steels' and stacks the same four aging states (as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h).
The labelled reflections in both panels are (111)γ, (110)δ, (200)γ, (200)δ, (220)γ, (211)δ, (311)γ and (222)γ — i.e. two phases, austenite (γ) and ferrite (δ), are identified by peak indexing.

The strongest peaks in both panels occur in the lowest-angle cluster immediately above the 40° gridline, with much weaker reflections near 65°, 82° and 90-95°; no peak positions are printed numerically.
Within each panel the four stacked patterns (as-cast vs the three aged states) show no visible change in peak position or relative peak height.
The third image is an as-cast micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar, annotated 'as-cast', showing a grey matrix labelled γ and darker, partly lamellar/dendritic constituents labelled δ.
The caption states the figure shows 'XRD patterns of the a) 0.02Nb steels and b) 0.04Nb steels, at different aging states'.
The citing text states that the microstructure of all the Nb-containing steels consists of ferrite and austenite.
The citing text states that after aging at different temperatures the diffraction peak intensity of both austenite and ferrite in the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels shows almost no significant change.
The citing text states that retention of metastable austenite at room temperature after near-rapid solidification and cooling has been observed in Figure 1 and 2.
The citing text states that increased Nb content and the aging treatments have minimal impact on the constituent phase fraction and its chemical compositions (Figure 1, Figure 2 and Table 4).
The figure itself does not print any d-spacing, lattice parameter or phase-fraction value; the γ/δ identification rests on the printed reflection indices alone.

subfigures.description: Stacked XRD patterns of the 0.02Nb steels, Intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ = 30-100°, four curves offset vertically (as-cast black, 723 K/3 h red, 773 K/3 h blue, 823 K/3 h green). Reflections indexed (111)γ, (110)δ, (200)γ, (200)δ, (220)γ, (211)δ, (311)γ, (222)γ; peak positions and heights are nearly the same in all four aging states.

Stacked XRD patterns of the 0.04Nb steels, same axes (Intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ = 30-100°) and same four aging states (as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h) with the identical γ/δ reflection indexing as panel (a); no visible change in peak intensity or position with aging.

As-cast micrograph annotated 'as-cast', 20 µm scale bar, grey matrix labelled γ with darker partially lamellar/dendritic regions labelled δ; yellow arrows point to δ and to a lamellar colony, one purple arrow points at an unlabelled feature.

unreadable_items: The purple arrow in the as-cast micrograph points at a feature whose identity is not labelled and cannot be determined from the pixels.
The absolute 2θ positions of the indexed peaks are not printed as numbers; only relative positions against the 10° gridlines can be read.
The third image carries the panel letter '(a)', duplicating panel (a) of the XRD series; its original figure numbering (Figure 1 vs Figure 2) is not resolvable from the image alone.
